newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ bond yields fall despite "ugly" jobs number.
newsitem.headline: NZ bond yields fall despite "ugly" jobs number.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close

* Bond yields fall but bank bills higher
* Jobs growth 0.8 percent in Sept Qtr vs forecast 0.2 pct
* Easing in December still seen on agenda
New Zealand bond yields closed lower on Friday despite a jobs number described as "ugly".

Dealers said the initial reading was that jobs growth in the September quarter was as high as the Reserve Bank forecast for the year, but a closer inspection found that all the new jobs were part-time and full-time job numbers fell 0.8 percent.
"It's been a good performance considering we had an ugly employment number," a senior bond trader said.
There was buying in a flow-driven afternoon market in the short-dated bonds.
"There was a wave of buying in the short bonds. I can only assume another euro is planned," he said.
Dealers said that all the attention would go onto wages data due later this month but most traders expect the Reserve Bank to ease in its December 17 Monetary Policy Statement.

"People were shocked initially at the employment growth being so large but then they saw it was all part-timers and there was a sense of relief. The market rallied back," said a Wellington bank chief dealer.
Some observers believe the Reserve Bank may hold off again with its long-awaited easing until a government has been formed following the inconclusive election a month ago.
"I think as long as the wages data is fine, they will ease regardless of whether a government is formed, given that the currency is up where it is," the chief dealer said.
He said money aggregates had been coming off in the last three months and retail sales data had been weakening.

"If the wages data is positive in a couple of months it's going to be very hard for them not to ease but they may well tag it to risks in the construction and property sectors along with potential fiscal slippage.
"When you go through the checklist, everything is looking pretty rosy for them in terms of potential for them to ease."
However, bill traders said any easing was likely to come after the December futures close out in mid-December.
There was heavy volume in the December contract which ended down three points at 91.40 on volume of 4407. The contract got sold quickly down to a low of 91.31 before it staged a recovery.
Dealers expect the market next week to be in a holding pattern with direction dictated by the U.S. market and flows.
